pr_title: Validate versions for CCR snapshot on matching index version.
pr_body:
RestoreService will validate the snapshot based on max index version. However, we do not increment index version on patch releases. 

To prevent attempting to restore an index of a future patch release, this change will reject the restore already when building the snapshot info from newer nodes matching the current index version.

Related to https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/105295
Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/104620
pr_comments:
The `elasticsearch-ci/8.12.2 / bwc` failure is unrelated:
> [MixedClusterEsqlSpecIT » test {stats.EvalOverridingKey SYNC}](https://gradle-enterprise.elastic.co/s/zejgk2olzmdjg/tests/:x-pack:plugin:esql:qa:server:mixed-cluster:v8.12.2%23javaRestTest/org.elasticsearch.xpack.esql.qa.mixed.MixedClusterEsqlSpecIT/test%20%7Bstats.EvalOverridingKey%20SYNC%7D)

> We'll have to revisit this when we remove or change Node#getVersion, but I think this is good as a test fix.

Do we need to reassess the plans for this given the requirements for CCR (validate patch version constraint if index version matches)? The only alternative I see would be reverting to storing the actual version in the index metadata.

It seems to me like a very similar use case to persisted NodeMetadata. For stateful `Elasticsearch`, I don't see why we couldn't use `BuildVersion` or a class very much like it to wrap a `Version` identifier. Perhaps we could have a pluggable `CcrVersion` that wraps `Version` in stateful Elasticsearch, and wraps `IndexVersion` in stateless? Does that seem like it could work?

>  I don't see why we couldn't use BuildVersion or a class very much like it to wrap a Version identifier

That's pretty much what I'm using, just that build version isn't returned from DiscoveryNode (yet):
```
BuildVersion.fromVersionId(node.getVersion().id)
```

So maybe we should plan for `DiscoveryNode.getVersion()` to return `BuildVersion` mid/long term?

> So maybe we should plan for `DiscoveryNode.getVersion()` to return `BuildVersion` mid/long term?

Possibly -- `ServerlessBuildVersion` is intended to be a no-op (assuming the orchestration we control never tries to roll back a node in place), and we may want different behavior for Serverless CCR. Or perhaps we'll control things on the orchestration layer so that we avoid CCR incompatibilities between clusters, though I'm not sure how that would actually work, which would let us use the `BuildVersion` no-op in Elasticsearch.

All of that seems beyond the scope of this PR, though, and we'll catch it when we try to get `Version` out of `DiscoveryNode`.
This needs the changes in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/105657 (and dependent PRs) before this can be merged
@thecoop This should also work without bumping the version on a new release as it's falling back to build / release version if the index version matches. But happy to wait if you prefer.
It's more the comment does not match current reality - either we can fix it and update the comment later, or wait until the build infra changes are merged

Hi @thecoop , I initially wanted to mute in 8.12 thinking it was main, without having realized the 8.13 label was out a couple of days ago. So my original PR merged in main. Then I manually muted on 8.12. But I did not take further action because I thought any bug would be in both 8.12 and main. That's not the case?

This test fails on 8.12 branch, when upgrading from 8.12.0 to 8.12.1. It does not fail on main.

Is this test meant to check followers that differ only in patch versions can't update from leaders?

The index version on main has already been bumped, so this exception will be (correctly) hit. This implies that we need a new index version for _every single patch release_, rather than every minor release. Is that actually the case?
Yeah, it does follow that it checks patch releases too. We've had several discussions about this previously - I'll try and join these all up.

@rjernst @DaveCTurner We've had discussions previously about proactively bumping index versions in order to enforce version boundaries. Could you confirm that we still want to enforce CCR leader/follower boundaries down to the release patch version, which would require a new index version for every patch release? Or do we want to consider changing it to enforce it at the minor release version boundaries only?

IMO we do indeed want to remain strict here. I reckon it'd be good to find a different way to enforce that than creating a new `IndexVersion` for each patch release, but that seems like a valid workaround for now.

Very well.

However, there is a complexity here. 8.12 uses index version 8500008, so the new index version for 8.12.1 would be 8500009. **However**, that version has **already** been used as the first version for 8.13. So there is no space in the index version to allow 8.12.1+ to have different version numbers, to fix this test and enforce the patch version barrier.

We have updated IndexVersion to use similar numbering style as TransportVersion, to 8501000which does allow for patch versions, but that was only done _after_ 8.12 had been released.

**However**, I don't believe anything has actually changed for the recent index versions, and 8.13 hasn't been released yet, so 8500009 and 8501000 are actually identical. This means we could repurpose 8500009 for 8.12.1 (and the following numbers for 8.12.n), leaving 8.13, when it is released, on 8501000+.

I don't think this will actually change anything for serverless, as the format hasn't actually changed, and serverless knows nothing about releases.

So, to fix this:
- Re-designate version 8500009 as the version for 8.12.1, define it on 8.12 branch.
- Leave 8.13 on 8501000, rename the constant for 8500009 for 8.12.1 on main.

We would need to consider carefully how patch releases with automatic new index versions (and maybe transport versions) interact with versioning code, if anything actually changes about the index format.
